record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: A nice error basis is an orthogonal basis of d squared unitary operators on a d-dimensional Hilbert space whose products are basis elements up to phases, inducing an index group. A shift-and-multiply basis is obtained, in a suitable Hilbert-space basis, from products of permutation operators and multiplication operators. Is every nice error basis of shift-and-multiply type?

evidence.quote: The question that arises here is to decide whether every nice error basis is of shift and multiply type.

An answer to the question, given above, has recently be found by Andreas Klappenecker and Martin Roetteler. They show in their article “On the monomiality of nice error basis” [4] that there is in fact a nice error basis which is not of shift and multiplier type.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a $d$-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $U(\mathcal{H})$ denote the group of unitary operators on $\mathcal{H}$ equipped with the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product $\langle A,B\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(A^*B)$. A nice error basis on $\mathcal{H}$ is a collection $\mathcal{E} = \{E_g : g \in G\}$ of $d^2$ unitary operators indexed by a finite group $G$ of order $d^2$ such that:
(i) $E_e = I$, where $e$ is the identity of $G$;
(ii) $\operatorname{tr}(E_g) = 0$ for all $g \neq e$ (equivalently, the operators are orthogonal in the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product);
(iii) for all $g,h \in G$ there exists a phase $\omega(g,h) \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|\omega(g,h)| = 1$ such that $E_g E_h = \omega(g,h) E_{gh}$.
The group $G$ is called the index group of $\mathcal{E}$.

A shift-and-multiply basis (also called a monomial nice error basis) is a nice error basis $\mathcal{E}$ such that, in some orthonormal basis $\{|0\rangle, \ldots, |d-1\rangle\}$ of $\mathcal{H}$, every $E_g$ can be written as a product $P_\pi D$ of a permutation operator $P_\pi |k\rangle = |\pi(k)\rangle$ (for some permutation $\pi$ of $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$) and a diagonal unitary operator $D = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{d-1})$ with $|\lambda_k| = 1$ (i.e., every $E_g$ is a monomial unitary matrix in this basis).

Question: Is every nice error basis of shift-and-multiply type?
artifact.category_tag: Nice error bases in quantum information
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been resolved in the negative: Klappenecker and Rötteler proved that there exist nice error bases that are not monomial (i.e., not of shift-and-multiply type). Their construction provides explicit non-monomial examples; the smallest known counterexample arises in dimension d = 165.

status_evidence.title: On the Monomiality of Nice Error Bases
status_evidence.snippet: We exhibit a nice error basis of degree 165 that is not equivalent to a shift-and-multiply basis. Thus, not every nice error basis is of shift-and-multiply type.
status_evidence.claim: There exists a nice error basis that is not of shift-and-multiply (monomial) type, answering the question in the negative.
